newsitem.title: USA: Union slow-down hurts LA port loading-shippin exec.
newsitem.headline: Union slow-down hurts LA port loading-shippin exec.

text.p: A shipping executive said Tuesday that cargo-handling efficiency for his company has fallen 25 percent since October due to a deliberate slow-down by union workers in the Port of Los Angeles.

Karsten Lemke, vice president of Zim Container Services, said cargo loading productivity has slipped for his company and other West Coast operations since dockworker unions signed a contract in October, which changed dockworkers' payscale.
The International Longshoremen's and Warehousemen's Union could not be reached for comment.
"We are down 25 percent of normal productivity," Lemke said.

He confirmed a report in Tuesday's Wall Street Journal, which said productivity of essential container operations has slipped five to 30 percent as workers use "go-slow" tactics in the Los Angeles and San Francisco areas.
"The union felt they lost control," he said.
The combined ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach, Calif., are the world's third largest port complex, and West Coast ports handles about a third of U.S. shipping volume, he said.
